text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Shares closed higher for a second day, as pharmaceuticals were spurred higher by rising U.S. drug stocks and market nerves were steadied by a continued rebound on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,640.0, up 43.7 points, or 0.95 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares took heart, shrugging off a weak start on Wall Street in afternoon European trade to shoot ahead to new records amid comfortable liquidity conditions. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,798.51, up 42.69 points, or 1.14 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,819.52, up 58.45 points, or 1.55 percent.

PARIS - Stocks surged three percent to an all-time closing high, powered by gains on Wall Street, a rebound in the dollar and higher bond prices. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,867.44, up 82.68 points, or 2.97 percent.

ZURICH - Shares ended an active session at a record close, regaining strength after a closing dip the day before ended a four-day record run. The Swiss market index closed at 5,662.4, up 86.3 points, or 1.55 percent.

MILAN - Stocks closed sharply higher just below new record highs set on the all-share and blue chip indices during a session of active trading, but slightly lower volume than on Tuesday. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,469, up 153 points, or 1.15 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares swept higher over a broad front to close at a new all-time record in hectic trade, with Wall Street's softer opening only briefly denting investor enthusiasm. The AEX index closed at 871.46, up 10.40 points, or 1.21 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks posted healthy gains by the close as investor confidence in Japan's economic outlook was wafted higher by a surprisingly strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the key "tankan" survey by the Bank of Japan, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,679.27, up 337.34 points, or 1.66 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed sharply higher following the recovery on Wall Street and brokers said the market had more upside before it closed for the handover festivities next week. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,065.02, up 174.06 points, or 1.17 percent.

SYDNEY - Shares ended firmer and near their highs, the market climbing above the key 2,700 level after the Wall Street market staged an amazing recovery on Tuesday. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 16.7 points higher at 2,705.1 just 9.1 points short of its all-time record high of 2,714.2 set on June 20.

JOHANNESBURG - The all-share index ended at an all-time high, its second consecutive closing peak boosted by a strong recovery on Wall Street on Tuesday and better-than-expected local inflation data. The All-share index closed at 7,354.0, up 20.4 points, or 0.28 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,007.4, down 11.2 points, or 0.53 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,669.9, up 45.7 points, or 1.10 percent.
